content.value_statement: Convex projects span functions, schemas, realtime, storage, agents, and security, so teams can lose time choosing guidance. This skill maps each request to the right specialized Convex skill and documentation source.
actual_capabilities: Routes core development requests to function, schema, realtime, and HTTP action skills.
Points data and storage work toward file storage and migration skills.
Directs advanced patterns to agents, cron jobs, and component authoring skills.
Identifies security review routes for quick checks and deeper audits.
Provides quick-start ordering and links to Convex documentation.
limitations: It is an index skill, not a full tutorial for every Convex feature.
It depends on companion Convex skills being installed or available.
It does not run Convex commands or inspect project configuration by itself.
Documentation links may require internet access.

use_cases.title: Start a Convex feature
use_cases.description: Identify whether to use functions, schema, realtime, or HTTP action guidance before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan data changes
use_cases.description: Find the right storage or migration guidance before changing data models.

use_cases.title: Review production readiness
use_cases.description: Route security work to quick checks or deeper audit guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starting point
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right Convex skill for building a query, mutation, and schema for a simple feature.

prompt_templates.title: Map feature guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: I need realtime updates and file uploads in a Convex app. Route me to the right guidance and order of work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Convex migration from an old schema to a new validator model. Include the companion skills I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Convex architecture for backend, agents, cron jobs, HTTP actions, storage, and security gaps. Route each gap to the best companion skill.

output_examples.input: I need database validators for a new feature.
output_examples.output: Use the schema validator guidance first, then move to function guidance for queries and mutations.

output_examples.input: I want subscriptions and file uploads in one workflow.
output: Start with realtime guidance for subscriptions.
Use file storage guidance for upload and serving behavior.
Check best practices before combining both paths.

output_examples.input: I need a security review before launch.
output_examples.output: Use the security check path for a quick pass, then use the security audit path for a deeper review.

best_practices: Start with best-practices guidance for broad design, then move to feature-specific skills.
Choose the narrowest skill that matches the current task.
Use official documentation links for version-specific behavior.
anti_patterns: Asking this index for complete implementation details for every Convex feature.
Using advanced agent or cron guidance before defining schema and function boundaries.
Treating documentation links as project-specific proof without checking the repository.

faq.question: Is this a full Convex tutorial?
faq.answer: No. It is an index that routes tasks to focused Convex skills and documentation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute Convex commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and routing text only.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: It is most useful when the referenced companion Convex skills are available.

faq.question: Can it help with security work?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs users to quick security checks and deeper security audit guidance.

faq.question: What documentation does it point to?
faq.answer: It points to the primary Convex documentation and an LLM-optimized documentation file.
